pages: Odysseus fashioned a grappling hook from his dagger and a length of rope, preparing to climb the great boulder that blocked their only way out.
His plan was simple yet clever, but it would require them to risk everything...
As Polyphemus slept, Odysseus climbed the great boulder with a sharpened log in his hands.
Below him, his remaining men hid themselves amongst the sheep, waiting for the Cyclops to awaken and open the cave.
All they could do now was wait for their chance to escape...
At last, Polyphemus awoke and approached the entrance of the cave, unaware of the men hiding amongst his sheep.
With his great strength, the Cyclops began to move the boulder aside, slowly opening the only path to freedom.
Odysseus clung to the boulder, waiting for the moment to strike...
Before Polyphemus could leave the cave, Odysseus leapt from the boulder and onto the Cyclops.
With all his remaining strength, he drove the sharpened log into the Cyclops' single eye, blinding the monstrous shepherd.
The Cyclops cried out in agony, but Odysseus and his men had already begun their escape...
Odysseus and the few men that remained rushed from the cave, escaping beneath the cover of the fleeing sheep.
But as they reached the shore, Odysseus stopped and looked back upon the cave where so many of his men had died.
Behind him, the blinded Cyclops cried out to his father... Poseidon...
